skill.name: widgets-ui
skill.description: Render structured JSON widget definitions as interactive React and Next.js UI blocks for forms, cards, layouts, and data display.
skill.summary: Build interactive React widgets from structured JSON responses.
skill.author: inferen-sh

security_audit.summary: I confirmed the user-facing npx install blocks and the remote registry URL as supply-chain risks because they can fetch or install external components when followed. The remaining static hits are Markdown fences, inline code, examples, documentation links, image references, or placeholders. No prompt injection, credential access, or hidden malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Add explicit review guidance before running the shadcn install command, and pin package or registry versions where possible.
Present related skill installs as optional links, and require explicit user confirmation before any npx skills add command is run.

finding_verdicts.reason: The fenced bash Quick Start includes npx shadcn@latest add with a remote registry URL, which executes a package manager if followed. It is documented rather than automatic, so the risk is supply-chain exposure.

content.value_statement: Agent responses often need richer interfaces than plain text. This skill shows how to render structured widget JSON as React and Next.js UI components.
actual_capabilities: Shows a shadcn registry command for adding the widget renderer.
Demonstrates WidgetRenderer usage with typed Widget and WidgetAction values.
Documents layout, typography, interactive, and display widget types.
Provides flight card and contact form widget examples.
Shows an action handler pattern for submit and click actions.
limitations: Requires a React or Next.js project that can use shadcn components.
Depends on external ui.inference.sh resources for installation and documentation.
Does not provide a complete application scaffold or backend workflow.
Application code must validate untrusted widget data and handle actions safely.

use_cases.title: Render Agent Forms
use_cases.description: Create interactive form widgets from structured agent output for contact, intake, or feedback flows.

use_cases.title: Display Dynamic Cards
use_cases.description: Turn data from assistants into compact visual cards for bookings, summaries, and status panels.

use_cases.title: Prototype Generative UI
use_cases.description: Explore JSON-driven user interfaces before committing to custom React component designs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Widget
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a basic rendered widget.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use widgets-ui to create a simple text and button widget for a React page. Explain the widget structure in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Form Widget
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate form design with action handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use widgets-ui to design a contact form widget with name, email, message, and submit action. Include validation considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Data Card
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate display widget for structured data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use widgets-ui to plan a travel booking card with route, status, timing, and a clear primary action.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Widget Schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of generated UI before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned widget schema for usability, accessibility, action handling, and unsafe external content before implementation.

output_examples.input: Create a booking summary widget for a flight from SFO to JFK.
output_examples.output: A compact card layout with departure, arrival, flight status, timing details, and one clear action for viewing the itinerary.

output_examples.input: Plan a lead capture form for a product demo request.
output_examples.output: A form structure with contact fields, a message area, consent checkbox, submit action, and notes about server-side validation.

output_examples.input: Review a generated widget before adding it to my app.
output_examples.output: A concise review covering supported widget types, missing labels, unsafe image sources, and action handling responsibilities.

best_practices: Review remote registry content before running installation commands.
Validate widget data from agents before rendering it in production.
Keep action handlers narrow, explicit, and tied to known application workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not render untrusted image URLs without validation or proxying.
Do not let generated widgets trigger privileged actions without confirmation.
Do not treat example schemas as a complete security or accessibility model.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build React and Next.js interfaces from structured widget JSON, including forms, cards, layouts, and buttons.

faq.question: Does it install components automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands that a user or agent may run after review and confirmation.

faq.question: Which projects can use it?
faq.answer: It fits React or Next.js projects that can use shadcn-style component registry additions.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it validate widget JSON?
faq.answer: The skill explains widget shapes, but application code must validate data before rendering.

faq.question: What security review is needed?
faq.answer: Review remote install content, validate generated widget data, and require confirmation for sensitive actions.
